source.title: Encapsulation of primary dopaminergic neurons in a GDNF-loaded collagen hydrogel increases their survival, re-innervation and function after intra-striatal transplantation

material: GDNF-loaded type 1 bovine collagen hydrogel (2 mg/ml) cross-linked with 4 mg/ml 4s-StarPEG, encapsulating E14 VM cells

formulation.evidence: encapsulated in a GDNF-loaded (1000 ng) type 1 bovine collagen hydrogel (2mg/ml), cross-linked with 4s-StarPEG (4mg/ml)
encapsulated in a GDNF-loaded (1000 ng) type 1 bovine collagen hydrogel (2mg/ml), cross-linked with 4s-StarPEG (4mg/ml)
encapsulated in a GDNF-loaded (1000 ng) type 1 bovine collagen hydrogel (2mg/ml)
Primary dopaminergic neurons (400,000 cells) dissected from the VM of E14 foetuses were encapsulated

processing.evidence: Infusions were completed at a total volume of either 3 µl (6-OHDA lesion and MSC transplants) or 6 µl (VM transplants and collagen hydrogels) at a rate of 1 µl/min

degradation_time.evidence: The absence of collagen immunohistochemical staining 12 weeks post intra-striatal delivery showed that the collagen hydrogel is biodegradable at the implanted site (not shown).

biology.cell_type: E14 rat ventral mesencephalon dopaminergic neurons

other_outcomes.evidence: the delivery of cells in a GDNF-loaded collagen hydrogel resulted in a significant increase in the volume of striatal re-innervation (Fig. 7B,C; three-fold increase vs. VM alone)
other_outcomes.name: striatal re-innervation volume vs VM alone

survival.evidence: when cells were delivered in a GDNF-loaded collagen hydrogel there was a significantly greater level of cell survival (Fig. 7A,C; five-fold increase vs. VM alone)

notes: Transplanted into 6-OHDA lesioned rat striatum; 1.7-fold greater survival vs VM & GDNF; reduced microgliosis and astrocytosis; improved rotations at 9 and 12 weeks.
